'''Janet L. Scott''' (April 1964 – 23 January 2022) was a South African chemist who was Professor of Sustainable Chemistry at the [[University of Bath]]. She also worked as the Director of the [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]] Centre for Doctoral Training in Sustainable Chemical Technologies.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Changing Planet Seminar {{!}} Professor Janet Scott |url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/events/97156/changing-planet-seminar-professor-janet-scott/ |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=Imperial College London |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Scott was from [[South Africa]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The University is saddened to announce the death of Professor Janet Scott |url=https://www.bath.ac.uk/announcements/the-university-is-saddened-to-announce-the-death-of-professor-janet-scott/ |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=www.bath.ac.uk}}</ref> She studied chemistry and applied chemistry at the [[University of Natal]]. She moved to the [[University of Cape Town]] as a graduate student, where she earned a master's degree and a doctorate.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-02-09 |title=We regret the passing of Professor Janet Scott, CSCT Training Director - Centre for Sustainable and Circular Technologies |url=https://www.csct.ac.uk/prof-janet-scott/ |access-date=2023-06-07 |language=en-GB}}</ref> Her doctoral research considered [[cholic acid]] and methyl cholate.<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Inclusion compounds of cholic acid and methyl cholate|publisher=[publisher not identified]|date=1995|place=Place of publication not identified|language=English|first=Janet Lesley|last=Scott|oclc=890424475 }}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Scott joined the faculty at the [[University of Cape Town]] in 1992, where she worked until completing her doctorate in 1995. She joined the Fine Chemicals Corporation in South Africa in 1996. Scott moved to [[Monash University]] in 2000, where she worked as deputy director of the [[Australian Research Council]] Centre for Green Chemistry. In 2006 she was appointed a Senior [[Marie Curie Fellowship|Marie Curie Fellow]] at [[Unilever]].{{citation needed|date=February 2022}}

In 2010, Scott joined the Department of Chemistry at the [[University of Bath]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=The University is saddened to announce the death of Professor Janet Scott|url=https://www.bath.ac.uk/announcements/the-university-is-saddened-to-announce-the-death-of-professor-janet-scott/|access-date=2022-02-12|website=www.bath.ac.uk}}</ref> Her research considered renewable raw materials for the development of sustainable products. In 2011, she developed a biodegradable microbead that could be used to replace dangerous plastic [[microbead]]s.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Naturbeads – sustainable microbeads replace microplastics in cosmetics & toiletries|url=https://www.csct.ac.uk/casestudy/naturbeads-2/|access-date=2022-02-12|website=Centre for Sustainable and Circular Technologies|date=10 November 2020 |language=en-GB}}</ref> She was particularly interested in making microbeads from cellulose, an abundant natural material that does not derive from fossil fuels. For several years she developed a reliable, scalable strategy to generate cellulose microbeads.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Scientists make biodegradable microbeads from cellulose|url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/747696|access-date=2022-02-12|website=EurekAlert!|language=en}}</ref> She was made Reader in Sustainable Chemistry in 2016 and a Professor two years later.<ref name=":0" /> Scott launched Naturbeads, a spin off company for cellulose microbead generation, in 2018.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Biodegradable alternative to replace microplastics in cosmetics and toiletries|url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/714183|access-date=2022-02-12|website=EurekAlert!|language=en}}</ref> Naturbeads was supported by [[Innovate UK]]<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-11-11|title=Project aims to cut microplastics in pharmaceutical and chemical industries|url=https://www.csct.ac.uk/naturbeads-ukri-fund/|access-date=2022-02-12|website=Centre for Sustainable and Circular Technologies|language=en-GB}}</ref> and Sky Ocean Ventures.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Arthur|first=Andrew|date=2021-12-03|title=Bath Uni spin-out wins funding to help reduce plastic pollution|url=https://www.business-live.co.uk/technology/bath-university-spin-out-wins-22344540|access-date=2022-02-12|website=Business Live|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-08-09|title=Start-up develops biodegradable alternative to plastic microbeads|url=http://www.irishnews.com/magazine/science/2019/08/09/news/start-up-develops-biodegradable-alternative-to-plastic-microbeads-1681320/|access-date=2022-02-12|website=The Irish News|language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Scott left the [[University of Bath]] in 2020 due to ill health.<ref name=":0" /> She died in January 2022.<ref name=":0" />
